title: Dashboard entropy and untracked KV eviction events — instrumentation inventory & remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During the 2025-02-18 capacity incident (see postmortem), on-call identified multiple dashboard panels that were uncorrelated with the true failure modes. In particular, KV cache eviction activity was not being surfaced as a first-class metric and several dashboards used sampled traces that omitted the eviction path. This ticket is an inventory and remediation plan to make KV eviction and request-path telemetry first-class, reduce dashboard entropy, and add targeted alerts and synthetic checks so future incidents are detected and triaged faster.
root_cause: The runtime emitted internal KV cache evictions to local logs but never incremented a centralized metric (kv.cache.evictions) with tenant-scoped tags. Dashboards relied on inferred signals (heap pressure / queue depth) and a high-sampling trace policy that dropped eviction spans. During autoscale and noise, eviction-induced tail latency spikes were invisible in dashboards and alerts, delaying mitigation.
impact_summary: Delayed detection of sustained tail-latency regressions for a subset (~7%) of tenants experiencing cache churn. Manual pager escalations and runbook playbacks took ~18 minutes longer than target because eviction activity wasnt visible; some customer requests hit higher egress costs due to retries. No data exfiltration or security incidents.
action_items: Instrument a tenant-scoped metric: kv.cache.evictions{tenant_id, pool, eviction_reason} with a standardized unit (count) and add to metrics pipeline (statsd -> metrics-ingest).
Add a complementary histogram: kv.cache.eviction_latency_ms to capture time-to-eviction processing, to help correlate with request tail latencies.
Increase trace sampling for requests that hit eviction paths: add a tracepoint at kv::evict and force 100% sampling for traces that include that span for 14 days after deployment, then revert to 10%.
Revise the Console dashboard: create a dedicated KV Cache Health panel (heatmap of per-tenant eviction rate, per-pool eviction ratio, and eviction_reason breakdown).
Create an alert: alert if a tenants kv.cache.evictions rate increases > 5x baseline for 5m AND tail latency (p99) increases > 50ms over baseline; route to on-call + runtime-owner.
Add synthetic probe: daily synthetic workload that warms caches for a sample of tenants and validates expected eviction rates under no-load conditions; surface as a health-check boolean.
Backfill historical metrics: run a log-to-metric job on the last 90 days of archived logs to populate kv.cache.evictions and validate dashboard baselines.
Update runbooks: add section for eviction-driven tail and include steps to temporarily increase cache TTLs, throttle less-critical tenants, and fallback routes.
PR/QA checklist: unit tests for metric emission, integration test for trace sampling gating, and a small Canary rollout to staging followed by smoke checks.
Owner rotation: handoff instrumentation review to the runtime telemetry squad after initial rollout for ongoing maintenance.
acceptance_criteria: kv.cache.evictions emitted with tenant_id tag in prod and visible in metrics explorer for >90% of pods.
Console dashboard contains a KV Cache Health view with heatmap, time-series, and per-tenant drilldown.
Eviction-triggered traces are sampled and available in tracing UI; we can query traces that include kv::evict spans for a sample tenant.
Alert fires in staging under simulated eviction spike and routes correctly to the on-call rotation.
Historical baseline populated and automated dashboards update without manual rework.
decisions: Emit eviction metric via existing statsd shim to avoid adding new network paths (approved by infra).
Temporarily elevate trace sampling only for traces containing eviction spans to limit storage cost (14-day window).

Implement per-tenant tags on metrics but limit tag cardinality by restricting tenant tag to tiered bucket (enterprise, midmarket, self-serve) for aggregate alerting; full tenant_id kept for drilldown only.
Prioritize dashboard UX that surfaces heatmaps rather than dozens of per-tenant lines to reduce entropy.
